title: Emergent Intelligence
definition: The ability of a system to display intelligence that is not programmed into it, but rather arises from the interaction of its components.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Think of it like a game of chess. A single chess piece follows rules, but the game as a whole shows unexpected patterns and strategies that weren't programmed into the pieces.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: Emergent intelligence is a key concept in AI. It's when a system, composed of simple components, exhibits complex behavior that cannot be predicted from the individual components.
difficulty_levels.expert: Emergent intelligence is a fascinating phenomenon in AI, showing the limitations of top-down design approaches. It highlights the need for bottom-up approaches and the importance of understanding the system as a whole. It also connects to fields like complexity science and self-organization.

extra_fields.insight: The AI learned strategies in the games of Pong and Boxing that were not programmed into it, demonstrating emergent intelligence.
